title: Vatican II opens, 1962
hookLine: John XXIII calls a council to bring the Church up to date

lines: A POPE TO KEEP THE SEAT WARM.
A COUNCIL FOR THE WHOLE CHURCH.
cards: A new pope, and, the story goes, some expected him simply to keep the seat warm. A small group of cardinals in a Roman basilica, expecting a routine address.
Then he tells them he means to call a council for the whole Church. The room, it's said, went quiet.
The pope was John the Twenty-third, and the word that came to sum up what he wanted was Italian, his own language: aggiornamento.

teach.b: Aggiornamento means bringing up to date. Not replacing, not starting over: updating, the way a family updates an old house it still loves.
On the day the council opened, John the Twenty-third gave a speech known by its first Latin words, Gaudet Mater Ecclesia, Mother Church rejoices. Three things in it are worth carrying.
First, he said he disagreed with the prophets of doom, people who could see nothing in the modern world but ruin. He wanted a council that looked at its own age with hope.
Second, he drew a distinction that shaped everything after: the ancient teaching of the faith is one thing; the way it is put into words is another. The substance stays.
The way of speaking can change, so that people today can actually hear it. That is aggiornamento in a sentence.
Third, he said the Church today would rather use the medicine of mercy than of severity. Now the well-known picture.

People like to say he was asked what the council was for, walked to a window and threw it open, to let in fresh air. It's a story people tell. It isn't in the speech, and it may never have happened as told.
But it stuck, because it pictured what he'd actually said. The Book of the Apocalypse, in the Douay-Rheims, has God say, "Behold, I make all things new." Not all new things: all things, new.

how: Catholics remember the Second Vatican Council through its documents, read in parishes and schools, and the word aggiornamento is still used when describing how the Church presents its unchanging faith to each new age.

o: bringing the Church up to date, same faith
replacing old teaching with new teaching
a council called to condemn the modern world

s: the open-window line is in John XXIII's opening speech
it's a story people tell; the speech itself doesn't contain it.
John XXIII said the substance of the faith differs from the way it is worded
that distinction, in Gaudet Mater Ecclesia, is aggiornamento in a sentence.
aggiornamento meant replacing the old faith with a new one
it means updating: the same faith, put into words people today can hear.

games.q: you're a pope opening a council. some advisers see only ruin in the modern world. what do you tell the bishops?
o: agree, and call the council to condemn the age.
disagree with the prophets of doom, and choose mercy.
postpone the council until times improve.
games.why: John XXIII said he disagreed with the prophets of doom and that the Church would rather use the medicine of mercy than severity.

practice: If there's a window near you, open it, even a crack, or a door, or just turn toward the light, and notice the air coming in: its temperature, its smell, sounds that weren't in the room a minute ago.
Nothing in the room has been thrown out; it's the same room, with air. If you pray, let the air carry a prayer for the Church.

wordCard.voice: Aggiornamento. Italian for bringing up to date: the same faith, put into words people today can hear. Today's word.

orig.note: Italian, bringing up to date; the word became shorthand for John XXIII's hope for the council.

carryVoice: Your line: open the windows. Fresh air, without throwing out what you love. That's day seven hundred ninety.

sources.q: Behold, I make all things new.
